⭐ **Top 3 du jour à publier**
**1**) **The Giants Never Fell. The Bounce Belongs to Laggards.**
The index is the wrong tool because the few giants propping it never fell, so the bounce goes to the laggards. I own equal-weight S&P 𝟱𝟬𝟬 against the cap-weighted index; I am wrong if the 𝟱𝟬-day reading keeps sliding.
**2**) **Stocks Are 2.7 Points From 1999. Bonds Stay Scarce.**
Credit should crack, yet stock this dear is the cheapest money boards have, so they sell shares and keep bonds scarce. I own corporate bonds against the index, and a Shiller P/E above the 𝟰𝟰.𝟮 record proves me wrong.
**3**) **Stocks Trade at 2.2 Times 2000. Bonds Hold the Risk.**
That price needs record margins forever, and lenders carry that bet without the upside, so credit holds the worse side. I own the S&P 𝟱𝟬𝟬 against corporate bonds, and price to sales back below 𝟯.𝟬𝟰 proves me wrong.
